record.title: Anthropic publishes a Claude-attributed subexponential #3-SAT algorithm claim with Lean materials
record.summary: Anthropic contributed a version-one preprint on October 27 describing a deterministic algorithm that counts satisfying assignments for fixed-width CNF formulas in subexponential time, including #3-SAT, and attributes the core algorithm to an internal Claude research model. Anthropic’s official repository includes the paper and a Lean 4 formalization. GitHub reports that the repository’s exact commit passed its `verify (eth)` CI workflow, which the README describes as a pinned Lean build, Comparator check and nanoda recheck. This repository-hosted result was not independently rerun here. The README explicitly says machine checks do not establish that the formal statement matches the paper; independent mathematical review remains open. The result is asymptotic and does not establish practical SAT performance. An independent external formal-methods audit later reports replaying Anthropic's exact pinned Lean proof with Lean, Comparator and nanoda, a fresh-environment replay, and a Lean bridge from the formal statement to textbook-style ETH in Anthropic's own machine model. The auditor explicitly leaves paper-to-statement and machine-model/input-encoding correspondence to prose and does not certify the paper's mathematical argument. This strengthens the reported reproducibility of the formal artifact, not the truth status of the theorem.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Anthropic contributed a v1 preprint on Hexagon dated October 27, 2026, and its official GitHub repository provides the paper and Lean 4 materials.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Anthropic reports that an internal Claude model found a deterministic subexponential-time algorithm for exact #3-SAT counting; the result would refute ETH if the paper’s argument and scope are correct.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper’s provenance statement says the core algorithm was found on October 16 by an internal Claude research model with 14 million output tokens and no human input, after which Anthropic researchers worked with Claude on presentation.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Anthropic’s official README documents Lean 4.33.1/Mathlib and a Comparator/nanoda check; GitHub reports that the `verify (eth)` workflow completed successfully on exact commit 16a5ce4. These are repository-reported verification results, not an independent proof review or rerun. The README explicitly says machine checks do not establish that the formal statement matches the paper.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: No practical SAT-solving performance, measured algorithmic speedup, or independent mathematical acceptance is established. Repository CI reports a successful formal check, but the statement-to-paper correspondence and correctness of the novel argument remain open.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: An external formal-methods auditor reports replaying Anthropic's exact pinned Lean proof with Lean's kernel, Comparator and nanoda, plus a fresh-environment replay, and proving a Lean bridge from Anthropic's formal statement to textbook-style ETH in Anthropic's own machine model. The report explicitly leaves the paper-to-statement and machine-model/input-encoding correspondence to prose; it does not certify the mathematical argument or the paper's claim.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The external auditor now reports Lean-checked bridges from Anthropic’s formal statement to textbook ETH in its stated machine model and to a standard multitape Turing-machine formulation with binary encoding. The auditor says the final identification with textbook ETH remains a reading; the audit does not machine-check correspondence between the printed paper theorem and the formal statement or certify the mathematical argument.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent complexity theorist has certified the tensor-contraction argument or established that the printed paper theorem is correctly represented by the Lean statement. An external audit reports kernel-checked proof and model bridges, but explicitly leaves the paper-to-statement relation as human reading.

The independent audit now reports a Lean-checked bridge from Anthropic’s formal statement through its own machine model to a standard multitape Turing-machine/binary-encoding statement. It does not machine-check the correspondence between the printed paper theorem and Lean statement; the final identification with textbook ETH remains a reading.
No measured performance on practical SAT instances is reported; the repository characterizes the result as purely asymptotic.

brief.importance_rationale: If correct, deterministic subexponential exact counting for fixed-width k-CNF would contradict ETH and require reassessment of many conditional lower-bound results. This score represents consequence if true, not confidence; independent review is absent and practical impact is not shown.
limitations: This is an Anthropic-attributed preprint claim, not an independently accepted theorem.
Lean checks a formal statement; the repository explicitly leaves paper-to-statement correspondence to human inspection.
The source says the result is asymptotic and says nothing about solving formulas in practice.
The similar OpenAI claim is a separate event and does not corroborate Anthropic’s result.
The exact repository commit has a successful source-reported verify (eth) CI run, but no independent rerun or mathematical proof review is established.
The repository explicitly leaves the correspondence between its checked formal statement and the paper to human review.

An external auditor reports replaying the exact pinned Lean artifact and formalizing a bridge from its statement to textbook-style ETH within Anthropic's own machine model. The report leaves paper-to-statement and cross-model correspondence to prose and is not a correctness verdict.

technical.claimed_result: Anthropic claims its internal Claude research model found a deterministic subexponential algorithm for exact #3-SAT counting, which refutes ETH. The paper states a 2^{O(n log log n / sqrt(log n))} time form for fixed-width counting; correctness and its precise correspondence to standard ETH remain subject to independent review.
technical.compute_or_cost: No compute or token cost is reported in the inspected README beyond a provenance claim of 14 million model output tokens; that figure is not independently measured here.
technical.demonstrated_result: Anthropic’s v1 paper and official ETH repository are public. The repository is pinned here to commit 16a5ce41304fcdaea4e0be7c132e1c361dc26da5. GitHub reports that the exact commit’s `verify (eth)` Actions check completed successfully; the README documents that workflow as Lean compilation, Comparator statement checks and nanoda rechecking. This is a source-reported CI result; this activation did not rerun it. The README expressly leaves paper-to-formal-statement correspondence to human review. An external auditor separately reports replaying the exact pinned Lean artifact with Lean's kernel, Comparator and nanoda and proving a formal bridge to textbook-style ETH inside Anthropic's own machine model. the research desk inspected that report but did not reproduce the runs; the auditor leaves paper-to-formal-statement and cross-model correspondence to prose.
technical.implementation_status: Research artifact and Lean 4 formalization are public. No practical solver deployment or measured runtime result is established.
technical.mechanism: The paper describes a tensor-network contraction method and derives an asymptotic subexponential bound for exact #k-SAT counting. The repository README gives a condensed tensor-contraction argument, but this activation did not inspect the full paper proof or independently derive the bound.
technical.novelty: The release is distinct from OpenAI’s concurrent ETH-refutation claim. The overlap does not establish independent correctness or identical algorithms.
technical.regime: Fixed clause width k, exact satisfying-assignment counting, and asymptotic input size. The README explicitly says the result does not establish practical performance.
technical.reproducibility: A date-matched immutable repository commit (16a5ce41304fcdaea4e0be7c132e1c361dc26da5) is available, and GitHub reports the exact commit’s `verify (eth)` check completed successfully at 2026-10-27T03:31:47Z. The README says this workflow pins Lean/Mathlib, builds the project, runs Comparator and checks with nanoda. The run was not independently reproduced here, and successful formal checking does not settle whether the formal statement matches the paper or whether the argument is mathematically sound. An external formal-methods report (Carlos Toledo, https://www.carlostoledo.co/eth/) says the Anthropic artifact was independently replayed from its pinned commit using Lean's kernel, Comparator and nanoda, then replayed in a fresh environment, and formally bridged to textbook-style ETH in Anthropic's own model. the research desk inspected the report but did not reproduce the runs. The report leaves the natural-language paper correspondence and machine-model/input-encoding step to prose; it is not an independent correctness verdict.
technical.strongest_baseline: ETH is the standard conjecture that 3-SAT requires 2^{Ω(n)} worst-case time. The paper presents an asymptotic contradiction, not a measured comparison on practical formulas.

brief.title: Anthropic publishes a Claude-attributed subexponential #3-SAT algorithm claim with Lean materials
brief.why_it_matters: If the claimed exact-counting algorithm is correct for the stated regime, it contradicts the Exponential Time Hypothesis and would affect research that relies on ETH-based lower bounds. The consequence is substantial, but the paper is a preprint, independent mathematical review is not established, and the source explicitly disclaims practical performance implications.

other.title: OpenAI releases a claimed AI-generated refutation of the Exponential Time Hypothesis with Lean formalization
other.summary: OpenAI reports that an internal model produced a refutation of the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH), then released a natural-language manuscript and Lean formalization. The linked Lean scope describes a subexponential exact-counting bound for fixed-k canonical k-CNF formulas, a formalized statement that would contradict ETH if its definitions and scope match the standard conjecture. OpenAI says an external group led by Russell Impagliazzo, Ramamohan Paturi and Ryan Williams will examine the result; the group’s participation is not certification. Independent mathematical review, a reproduced build and practical algorithmic consequences remain unestablished.
